The Chief Strength of the Egyptian Armies Lay in Their Cavalry.</title> <div sID="gen14869" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8887"/><hi type="bold">1. and stay on horses, and trust in chariots--</hi>In their level and fertile plains horses could easily be used and fed (<reference osisRef="Exod.14.9">Ex 14:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Kgs.10.28">1Ki 10:28</reference>). In hilly Palestine horses were not so easily had or available. The Jews were therefore the more eager to get Egyptian chariots as allies against the Assyrian cavalry. In Assyrian sculptures chariots are represented drawn by three horses, and with three men in them (see <reference osisRef="Isa.36.9">Is 36:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.20.7">Psa 20:7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Dan.9.13">Da 9:13</reference>). <div eID="gen14869" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 31 Is 31:1-9 . The Chief Strength of the Egyptian Armies Lay in Their Cavalry. 1. and stay on horses, and trust in chariots-- In their level and fertile plains horses could easily be used and fed ( Ex 14:9 ; 1Ki 10:28 ). In hilly Palestine horses were not so easily had or available. The Jews were therefore the more eager to get Egyptian chariots as allies against the Assyrian cavalry. In Assyrian sculptures chariots are represented drawn by three horses, and with three men in them (see Is 36:9 ; Psa 20:7 ; Da 9:13 ).
